problem.text: Square $ABCD$ has side length $1$. Points $P$, $Q$, $R$, and $S$ each lie on a side of $ABCD$ so that $APQCRS$ is an equilateral convex hexagon with side length $s$. What is $s$?

steps.title: Where to start: sketch the hexagon and find the lengths along the sides
steps.body: Two of the hexagon's corners, $A$ and $C$, are corners of the square. Going around $A \to P \to Q \to C$, the point $P$ sits on side $AB$ and $Q$ sits on side $BC$. So the hexagon sides $AP$ and $QC$ lie right along the square's sides, and each has length $s$.

your_turn.prompt: Side $AB$ has length $1$ and $AP = s$. What are $PB$ and $BQ$ in terms of $s$?

steps.title: Look at the corner triangle
steps.body: The hexagon cuts off triangle $PBQ$ at corner $B$. It has a right angle at $B$ and two legs of length $1-s$, so it is a right isosceles (45-45-90) triangle. Careful: the hexagon side $PQ$ is the slanted side, the hypotenuse, not a leg.

your_turn.prompt: In a right isosceles triangle with legs $L$, how long is the hypotenuse?

steps.title: Set up the equation
steps.body: So $PQ = \sqrt2\,(1-s)$. But $PQ$ is also a side of the equilateral hexagon, so it equals $s$: $$\sqrt2\,(1-s) = s.$$

your_turn.prompt: Move all the $s$ terms to one side. What equation do you get?

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: Divide and rationalize by multiplying top and bottom by $\sqrt2 - 1$: $$s = \frac{\sqrt2}{1+\sqrt2} = \frac{\sqrt2(\sqrt2-1)}{(\sqrt2+1)(\sqrt2-1)} = 2-\sqrt2.$$ Check: $s \approx 0.586$ and $1-s \approx 0.414$, and $0.414 \times 1.414 \approx 0.586$. The answer is **(C)** $2-\sqrt2$.

wrong_choices.B: This comes from treating $PQ$ as if it were a leg of the corner triangle, so $1-s = s$. But $PQ$ is the hypotenuse, which is $\sqrt2$ times the leg.
wrong_choices.A: This comes from assuming $A$, $P$, $Q$, $C$ lie on a straight line, so the three sides split the diagonal $AC = \sqrt2$ into thirds. But the path bends at $P$ and $Q$, so its length is more than the diagonal.

verification.verifier_notes: Passed adversarial verifier on first review.
